BC Geographical Names
notes: GEOGRAPHICAL NAMES ID is a system generated unique identification number for a geographical name, e.g., 53996

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: FEATURE ID is an identifier for a geographical feature that is unique within the the BCGNIS system. For example: 54321.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: FEATURE UUID is a Universally Unique IDentifier for a FEATURE that conforms to the RFC 4122 specification. The FEATURE UUID is stored as 32 hexidecimal digits. For example: 72fd7cc7c73b4b8dba286fe8988ddf50. This universally unique number was introduced to promote sharing and exchange of FEATURE …

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: GEOGRAPHICAL NAME is the officially-designated name assigned to the geographical feature, e.g., Arctic Lake Plateau.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: FEATURE TYPE is a specific or narrow classification for a geographical feature. FEATURE TYPEs are standardized across Canada. There are approximately 1500 distinct FEATURE TYPEs identified nationally, of which approximately 350 are presently in use in British Columbia, e.g., Stream, Lake, Village.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: FEATURE TYPE CODE is a system generated unique identification number that corresponds to the FEATURE TYPE. For example, the FEATURE TYPE CODE "2701" corresponds to the FEATURE TYPE "Mountain".

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: FEATURE CATEGORY is a Canada-wide, standardized classification which subdivides FEATURE CLASSes into physically-similar groups, e.g., Flowing Freshwater, Elevated Shoreline Features, Standing Water Surrounded by Land.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: FEATURE CLASS is a Canada-wide, standardized classification that separates geographical features into broad groupings based on geographical, cultural or thematic similarity, e.g., Populated, Administrative Areas, Water Features.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: LATITUDE is the geographic coordinate, in decimal degrees (ddd.dddddd), of the location of the feature as measured from the equator, e.g., 55.323653

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: LATITUDE DMS is the latitude of the feature in degrees, minutes, seconds (DMS) format. For example: "55 17 45 N" means 55 degrees, 17 minutes and 45 seconds North of the equator.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: LONGITUDE is the geographic coordinate, in decimal degrees (ddd.dddddd), of the location of the feature as measured from the prime meridian, e.g., -123.093544

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: LONGITUDE DMS is the longitude of the feature in degrees, minutes, seconds (DMS) format. For example: "121 28 14 W" means 121 degrees, 28 minutes and 14 seconds West of the prime meridian.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: DATUM is a set of reference points on the Earth's surface against which position measurements for LATITUDE and LONGITUDE are made, e.g., NAD27 or NAD83

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: POSITION TYPE is a descriptive word that explains the geographic positioning of the feature, e.g., Centre, Summit, Mouth.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: NTS MAPSHEET is the name of the NTS map that contains the geographical feature's coordinates, e.g., 93A/13.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: RELATIVE LOCATION is a brief description of the relative position of the geographical feature, e.g., W side of Shackleton Glacier in the Clemenceau Icefield, just E of Cummins Lakes Provincial Park.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: LAND DISTRICT is the name of the land district containing the geographical feature, as identified in Land Title records, e.g., Cassiar Land District.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: MIN SCALE DENOMINATOR is the denominator of the suggested minimum scale at which the geographical name for this feature should be visible on most maps. For example, 1000000 means the geographical name should not be displayed at scales smaller than 1/1000000.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: MAX SCALE DENOMINATOR is the denominator of the suggested maximum scale at which the geographical name for this feature should be visible on most maps. For example, 50000 means the geographical name should not be displayed at scales larger than 1/50000.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: FEATURE CODE contains a value based on the Canadian Council of Surveys and Mapping's (CCSM) system for classification of geographic features, e.g. FW84555210

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: GEOMETRY is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: OBJECTID is a column required by spatial layers that interact with ESRI ArcSDE. It is populated with unique values automatically by SDE.

dataset_title: BC Geographical Names
notes: SE ANNO CAD DATA is a binary column used by spatial tools to store annotation, curve features and CAD data when using the SDO GEOMETRY storage data type.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: COMMON_NAME_ENGLISH is the English name of the species or taxa listed on SARA Schedule 1; e.g., 'Sage Thrasher'.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: COMMON_NAME_FRENCH is the French name of the species or taxa listed on SARA Schedule 1; e.g., 'Moqueur des armoises'.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: COSEWIC_POPULATION is the population name of the species or taxa assessed by the Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada (COSEWIC) and currently listed on SARA Schedule 1; e.g., 'Southern Mountain population'.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: CRITICAL_HABITAT_REGION is a regional identifier optionally used to group critical habitat polygons; e.g. "Southeastern BC".

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: CRITICAL_HABITAT_SITE_ID is the alphanumeric code of a critical habitat site as defined in the federal recovery document; e.g., '937_5'.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: CRITICAL_HABITAT_SITE_NAME is the name of a critical habitat site as defined in the federal recovery document; e.g., 'Kilpoola'.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: CRITICAL_HABITAT_DETAIL is the level of detail of critical habitat polygon; e.g., 'Detailed polygon' or 'Grid square'. Grid squares are used when detailed polygons contain sensitive information that cannot be released.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: CRITICAL_HABITAT_APPROACH is the scale at which the polygons were defined and refers to processes within the Critical Habitat Toolbox policy; e.g., 'Landscape', 'Area' or 'Site'.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: CRITICAL_HABITAT_METHOD is a broad description of how the critical habitat was identified and refers to processes within the Critical Habitat Toolbox policy; e.g., 'Critical Function Zone'.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: CRITICAL_HABITAT_COMMENTS are notes about the critical habitat or specific polygon; e.g., 'Polygons were identified as part of a multispecies recovery plan'.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)
notes: CRITICAL_HABITAT_DATE_EDITED is the date that the polygon was last edited; e.g., '8/21/2014'.

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)

dataset_title: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk (posted)

Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: GW_WWL_SYSID is a system generated unique identification number

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: The file number assigned to a particular well in the in the province*s Groundwater Wells and Aquifers application, e.g., 56809.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Steel plate with a unique number that is attached to required wells under the groundwater protection regulations such as water supply wells, recharge or injection wells made by drilling or boring, and permanent dewatering wells, e.g., 691.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Street address of the property that the well is physically located on.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Description of the status of a well as defined in the Groundwater Protection Regulation of the Water Act, i.e. New, Abandoned, Alteration, Closure, Other.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Valid classification as defined in the Groundwater Protection Regulation of the Water Sustainability Act, i.e., Water Supply, Monitoring, Recharge, Injection, Dewatering, Drainage, Remediation, Geotechnical, Closed-loop geoexchange.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: The intended use of the water in a water supply well as reported by the driller at time of work completion on the well, e.g., private domestic, irrigation, water supply system, industrial commercial, unknown.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Description of valid licencing option granted to a well under the Water Water Sustainability Act. This information comes from eLicensing, i.e. Unlicensed, Licensed, Historical

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Link to the well summary report within the Groundwater Wells and Aquifer (GWELLS) application, which provides the overall desription and history of the well.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Depth below ground surface of the start of the lithology material for a particular lithology layer, as observed during the construction or alteration of a well, measured in feet.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Depth below ground surface of the end of the lithology material for a particular lithology layer as observed during the construction or alteration of a well, measured in feet.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Describes the standard terms used to characterize the different qualities of lithologic material, e.g. dry, loose, weathered, soft.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Description of the material noted for lithology. E.g. Rock, Clay, Sand, Unspecified.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: The colour of the lithologic material identified at time of drilling, e.g. black, dark, tan, rust-coloured

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: The hardness of the material that a well is drilled into (the lithology), e.g. Very Hard, Medium, Very Soft.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Free form text used by the driller to describe observations made of the well lithology including, but not limited to, the lithologic material.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Free form text used by the driller to describe observations made of the well lithology including, but not limited to, the lithologic material.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: The depth at which the well was *finished*, measured in units of feet bgl (below ground level), e.g. 157.0. It can be shallower than the total well depth which is the total depth at which the well was drilled.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: Depth below ground level at which bedrock starts, measured in feet, e.g. 132.0.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: An approximate estimate of the capacity of the well to produce groundwater. Estimated by the well driller during construction by conducting a well yield test.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: The unit of measure used for the well yield. As of April 2019 well yields are reported in U.S. Gallons per Minute. Prior to April 2019, well yield units vary or are unknown, e.g., U.S. Gallons per Minute, Gallons per Hour (U.S./Imperial), Dry Hole, Unknown Yield.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: The level (depth below top of casing) to which water will naturally rise in a well without pumping, measured in feet, e.g. 280.0

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: The diameter of the casing of the well, measured in inches, e.g. 6.62. There can be multiple casings in a well, e.g. surface casing, and production casing. Diameter of casing made available to the public is generally the production casing.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: System generated unique sequential number assigned to each mapped aquifer. The aquifer ID identifies which aquifer a well is in. An aquifer can have multiple wells, while a single well can only be in one aquifer.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: GEOMETRY is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: OBJECTID is a column required by spatial layers that interact with ESRI ArcSDE. It is populated with unique values automatically by SDE.

dataset_title: Lithology of Ground Water Wells
notes: SE_ANNO_CAD_DATA is a binary column used by spatial tools to store annotation, curve features and CAD data when using the SDO_GEOMETRY storage data type.
